newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold imports hit record 56.05 tonnes in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold imports hit record 56.05 tonnes in Feb.

text.p: Gold imports into Dubai, a major trading centre for the precious metal, more than doubled in February to a record 56.05 tonnes from 23.48 tonnes in the same month last year, the World Gold Council (WGC) said.
February's figure is a fresh monthly record after the previous high of 46.35 tonnes in January.
"The entire region is buying gold. India is buoyant and Pakistan is slowly returning to its old gold buying habits," regional WGC chief executive Rolf Schneebeli said on Wednesday.
"The Middle East and India region is the fastest growing region in terms of demand for gold and Dubai is playing the role of the perfect hub for supply," he added in a statement.
The WGC said Dubai imports in the first two months of this year -- at over 102 tonnes -- exceeded imports in the first quarter of last year at nearly 75 tonnes.

"Low gold prices have obviously played their part in making gold an even more attractive buy...Low prices have brought out the hoarding instinct in buyers who have taken advantage of attractive prices," said WGC Gulf manager D.V. Pathy.
The WGC said Dubai imported gold from 17 countries in February. Switzerland remained the top gold exporter to Dubai with 38.63 tonnes. Britain came next, followed by South Africa.
The Geneva-based WGC is a non-profit association owned by major gold producers and monitors about 75 percent of the world's markets. --Hilary Gush, Dubai newsroom +9714-626990
